jobs.title: Head of Machine Learning
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Head of Machine Learning based in Canada.

This is a senior engineering leadership role responsible for shaping and advancing machine learning initiatives across a high-growth technology environment. You will lead the development of ML-powered products that help businesses make smarter, more personalized customer engagement decisions. The role combines technical leadership, product strategy, team building, and hands-on influence over engineering standards. You will tackle complex challenges spanning personalization, recommendation systems, identity resolution, generative AI, and large-scale ML infrastructure. Working closely with engineering and product stakeholders, you will establish a strong technical vision while maintaining a pragmatic focus on business impact. This is an opportunity to build and scale an emerging ML function with significant ownership and long-term influence.

Accountabilities

Lead the technical vision, roadmap, and execution of machine learning products and initiatives, balancing ambitious innovation with pragmatic engineering decisions.
Guide the development of ML-powered capabilities such as personalization, product recommendations, probabilistic identity resolution, and generative AI.
Oversee the design and evolution of scalable machine learning infrastructure supporting model training and inference for large enterprise customers.
Improve the team's pace of execution through strong technical leadership, effective prioritization, and removal of organizational or engineering obstacles.
Establish and maintain high standards for reliability, operational excellence, incident management, and production readiness.
Build and grow the machine learning organization by identifying hiring needs, designing effective evaluation processes, and attracting high-impact talent.
Mentor engineers and managers, support career development, and foster a highly engaged, collaborative, and intellectually curious team culture.
Partner with product and engineering leadership to identify high-value opportunities where machine learning can create meaningful customer and business impact.

Requirements

Significant experience leading engineering or machine learning teams, with a strong track record of delivering technically complex products or platforms.
Deep expertise in machine learning and familiarity with areas such as recommendation systems, personalization, identity resolution, generative AI, or large-scale model infrastructure.
Strong software engineering foundations and the ability to engage credibly in technical architecture, system design, and engineering trade-offs.
Experience building and scaling reliable ML systems for production environments, including model training and inference infrastructure.
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous or complex problems into clear technical strategies, product roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
Strong people leadership skills, including hiring, mentoring, performance management, and developing high-performing engineering teams.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, product, and other business functions.
A pragmatic, impact-oriented mindset with the judgment to balance technical excellence, execution speed, reliability, and business priorities.
Intellectual curiosity and enthusiasm for exploring emerging technologies, particularly advances in machine learning and large language models.

Benefits

Competitive annual salary range of $230,000–$400,000 USD, with compensation designed to be location-independent under a remote-first model.
Meaningful equity compensation.
Fully remote work environment across North America.
Significant ownership and influence over the direction of machine learning initiatives and products.
Opportunity to solve complex ML challenges involving personalization, recommendations, identity resolution, generative AI, and scalable infrastructure.
Strong emphasis on professional growth, technical impact, and leadership development.
Opportunity to build and scale a high-impact machine learning organization within a rapidly growing technology environment.

How Jobgether Works

We use an AI-powered matching process
to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

Why Apply Through Jobgether?

Data Privacy Notice:
By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Employment Opportunity

Chief Financial Officer

Full-time Permanent

Position

Chief Financial Officer
Location

Port Alberni Government Office, with at least one business day per week at the Anacla Government Office
Option

Full-time Permanent
Reports to

Executive Director
Salary/Starting Wage

$142,800.00 - $173,400.00 per year, based on education, skills and experience
Benefits

Extended health benefits and other benefits

Function & Job Summary

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is the second highest member of the senior management team and is responsible for the overall financial health of Huu-ay-aht First Nations. Reporting to the Executive Director, the CFO leads financial planning and analysis, accurate financial reporting, financial risk management and investment decisions, working with department managers to align resources with the Nation’s financial goals. The CFO provides financial guidance to administration and leadership to support transparency, sustainability and sound financial management.

Key Accountabilities

Strategic Leadership and Financial Management

· Provide strategic leadership and direction for the Nation’s financial management and support initiatives in the Huu-ay-aht Strategic Plan.
· Lead financial planning, development, management, internal process auditing and reporting for HFN and its operating entities; support Finance Department staff and program and department managers in managing their financial affairs.
· Design, implement and sustain control systems for the effective administration of HFN finances and assets.
· Manage the Finance Department and its budget in accordance with Nation standards and performance expectations. Recruit, coach and support assigned staff, promoting a performance-focused environment aligned with HFN values, culture and business goals.

Financial Administration and Reporting

· Administer and monitor the financial system to ensure HFN finances are maintained accurately and promptly in accordance with established accounting practices and HFN policies and procedures.
· Lead preparation of the annual budget, prepare quarterly reports and report on variances.
· Implement financial policies and procedures, establish and maintain cash controls, and monitor cash reserves and investments.
· Coordinate, negotiate and communicate with outside agencies on funding reports, audits, certification and compliance reporting.
· Provide technical and financial assistance to the Finance Committee and Invested Wealth Committee, and advice on HFN Public Body operations and business ventures.
· Prepare and present regular and special financial reports, including annual audited financial statements, to the Executive Director, Finance Committee, Executive Council, HFN programs and departments, and the boards and management of external entities, as assigned.
· Submit required financial reports to funding agencies and coordinate the presentation of annual financial reports to Huu-ay-aht citizens, as assigned.

Accounting and Payroll

· Coordinate and oversee accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll and internal reporting.
· Ensure income statements, balance sheets and monthly financial statements are prepared accurately and on time; review and process month-end journal entries.
· Ensure the general ledger is maintained and reconciled accurately. Review revenues and expenses with the senior management team to confirm entries align with budgets and make adjustments as required.
· Conduct quarterly reviews of accounts payable master data and provide periodic review and guidance for longstanding contracts and recurring expenses.
· Ensure bank and investment statements are reconciled monthly, accurately and on time.
· Ensure biweekly payroll is processed accurately and on time, and annual T4 slips are completed accurately by the deadline. Maintain effective payroll policies and support the payroll team in meeting processing requirements and deadlines.
· Ensure credit card security and maintain and monitor the credit card program.
· Ensure transactions are properly recorded in the computerized accounting system, maintain the system, and maintain financial files and records.

Audits

· Coordinate internal preparation for year-end audits of HFN and its business entities. Liaise with auditors, the Finance team and external stakeholders, ensuring the audit team receives all requested information.
· Maintain records of audit reports, transactions and financial statements; ensure adherence to accounting principles and provide required day-to-day operational information to external auditors.
· Ensure accounting controls are in place and managed to support a successful audit process.

Property Tax Administration

· Oversee administration of the Property Tax Act, including preparation of the tax roll from the assessment roll.
· Deliver tax notices to owners or occupiers of taxable property and copies to holders of charges against the property, including amendments arising from revised or supplementary assessment rolls or subdivisions.
· Track and collect taxes, penalties and interest; process refunds and interest charges or payments; issue tax arrears notices and maintain a list of liens for unpaid taxes.
· Issue tax certificates and exemption certificates, provide exemption certificates to the assessor, and track homeowner and other grants.
· Prepare and submit a draft real property tax budget for the next fiscal year to the Huu-ay-aht Taxation Authority and, once approved, incorporate it into the annual budget under the Financial Administration Act.

Operational Requirements

· Valid Class 5 driver’s licence.
· Work from the Port Alberni Government Office, with at least one business day per week at the Anacla Government Office.
· Willingness to travel, including overnight and weekend travel and possible travel to the United States.
· Willingness and ability to work overtime, including evenings and weekends.
· Successful completion of background checks, employment verification, criminal record checks, reference checks, and education and credential verification.

Educational and Experience Requirements

· University degree in business administration, accounting, finance or a related discipline.
· Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) accreditation through a provincial or territorial accounting body.
· At least seven years of leadership experience in a company or government finance department or in financial administration, with a proven record of successfully leading Finance teams.
· Experience working with, or a sound understanding of, Indigenous communities, histories and values, and the opportunities and challenges faced by Indigenous Peoples in Canada.
· A Master of Business Administration (MBA) is an asset.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

· In-depth knowledge of finance, accounting and numeracy, with the ability to monitor, allocate and control finances on a large scale.
· Strong leadership and management skills, analytical ability, problem-solving skills and work ethic.
· Excellent oral and written communication and presentation skills; ability to interpret complex financial reports and explain financial analysis and projections clearly to stakeholders and colleagues.
· ʔiisaak / Greater Respect: Respect for the community and its people, traditional knowledge, the natural and metaphysical worlds, and other peoples and communities. Demonstrate service excellence and contribute to a safe, healthy and respectful workplace.
· ʔuʔaałuk / Taking Care Of: Care for present and future generations and the resources provided by the land, water and natural world. Use resources responsibly and adopt more efficient ways of working.
· Hišukma c̕awak / Everything is One: Recognize the interconnected and reciprocal relationships among people, the land and the wider world. Listen to and incorporate others' views, work collaboratively and value diversity.

How to apply

Apply with a cover letter and resume to Human Resources at hr@huuayaht.org or by fax to 250-728-1222.
Please include "Chief Financial Officer Job Posting" in the subject line.
Application deadline: October 20, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. Pacific time.
We thank all applicants for their interest. We will contact only those selected for an interview.
We may give preference to qualified Huu-ay-aht citizens and qualified Indigenous applicants, consistent with HFN hiring policy.
